verdicts.question: Is Karnataka's e-way bill limit for intra-state movement ₹50,000 for all goods (confirm from the e-way bill portal or a Karnataka notification), and is the SMS e-way bill facility enough for small yards? Do small yards need a GST filing partner (GSP) to generate e-way bills and e-invoices, and what do such services cost?
verdicts.problems: Verification could not be run on this machine: the session's WebSearch budget (200 of 200) was already spent before this sceptic pass started, and outbound fetches (curl/WebFetch) are refused, so none of the 16 cited sources could be re-found from a snippet in this run. Under the brief's rule (holds=true only if the source itself was found) the answer cannot be passed as-is. Beyond that, concrete problems: (1) The decision contradicts the answer: the body correctly says a bill is needed for consignments worth 'more than ₹50,000' (rule 138(1) says 'exceeding fifty thousand rupees'), but the decision tells the receipt screen to ask for a bill 'whenever consignment value is ₹50,000 or more'. (2) Every source entry is dated 'opened 29 Sep 2026' although pages could not be opened; the brief requires 'snippet:' prefixes and the date shown in the result. (3) The following figures are plausible but not confirmed by any snippet: the ₹10 crore turnover gate for direct NIC API access (the portal's gate has changed over time); the software prices (Vyapar Gold ₹799/₹4,799, Silver ₹699/₹4,399, myBillBook Pro Max ₹570/month, Zoho Books Standard ₹899/₹749, ClearTax from ₹7,777/month) and whether Zoho Books Standard really includes e-invoicing (Zoho has moved e-invoicing between tiers); GSTN e-invoice FAQ 'Q24' numbering. Arithmetic checks out (₹570 x 12 = ₹6,840). (4) A likely-missed development: GSTN/NIC opened a parallel E-Way Bill 2.0 portal (ewaybill2.gst.gov.in) on 1 July 2025 with cross-portal generation, updating and consolidation, which matters for a yard's fallback plan more than SMS does; from memory, not confirmed by snippet. (5) Against the founder's refined chain the answer only looks at the kabadiwala-to-yard leg. The legs that routinely exceed ₹50,000 and often cross state borders are L3 to L5 (yard to pre-processor, pre-processor to recycler or compounder, to manufacturer), where the national ₹50,000 inter-state threshold applies regardless of Karnataka's rule; bales sent to a pre-processor on a job-work basis and returned as flake or granule move on a delivery challan and, for inter-state job work, need an e-way bill whatever the value; and each processing output (main lot, saleable by-product lot, residual-waste lot to an authorised handler or TSDF) that leaves the plant separately is its own consignment for the threshold, with residual hazardous waste also needing the HOWM manifest, which is a different document. The pickup/receipt screen therefore needs an e-way bill field on every lot movement, not only on yard receipts.
verdicts.correction: Karnataka's intra-state e-way bill threshold is the national one: a bill is required for any movement of taxable goods in a consignment worth more than ₹50,000 (not ₹50,000 or more), with no higher Karnataka limit and no scrap carve-out; Karnataka switched intra-state bills on from 1 April 2018 (Finance Department notification FD 47 CSL 2017 of 23 March 2018). This could not be re-verified from a snippet in this run, so re-check it on ewaybillgst.gov.in or the CBIC e-way bill FAQ before the pilot; the rule has been stable since 2018 and no 2026 change is known. Practical points for the pilot: when a registered yard buys from an unregistered kabadiwala, the yard generates the bill as recipient and enters URP as supplier; loads on non-motorised carts and loads of ₹50,000 or less need no bill; Part B (vehicle) is not needed for a consignor-to-transporter leg under 50 km inside the state. The SMS mode (register up to two mobiles per GSTIN, text 77382 99899 with EWBG/EWBV/EWBC) is free and official but is a backup only: one bill per message, no printout, and since 1 April 2025 every user also needs 2FA (SMS OTP, Sandes or NIC-GST-Shield). The main free tools are the NIC web portal and the parallel E-Way Bill 2.0 portal (ewaybill2.gst.gov.in, opened 1 July 2025 so bills can be raised, updated and consolidated on either portal when one is down; confirm this from a GSTN advisory), the IMEI-registered Android app and the Excel bulk tool; a bill cannot be raised on a document older than 180 days (from 1 January 2025). No GSP is needed: direct NIC API access is gated by turnover (the exact gate, said to be ₹10 crore, was not confirmed), and everyone else who wants software integration uses a GSP-backed product, but the portal, SMS and app work without one. E-invoicing applies only where aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18 (Notification 10/2023-Central Tax, effective 1 August 2023), and reverse-charge self-invoices for purchases from unregistered sellers are not e-invoiced, so it is irrelevant to small yards. Software cost figures (Vyapar, myBillBook, Zoho Books, TallyPrime, ClearTax) were not confirmed from any snippet in this pass: treat them as indicative only, re-open the vendor pricing pages before recommending one, and set status to 'partly'. Refined chain: the ₹50,000 rule bites mostly on L3 to L5 legs (yard to pre-processor, pre-processor to recycler/compounder, to manufacturer) and on inter-state movements, where the national ₹50,000 threshold applies everywhere; bales sent for job-work conversion move on a delivery challan and need an e-way bill for any inter-state job work regardless of value; and each processing output lot (main output, by-product, residual waste) leaving separately is its own consignment, with residual hazardous waste to a TSDF also carrying the HOWM manifest. Decision: do not build e-way bill generation in the pilot; put an optional 12-digit e-way bill number field on every lot movement (not just yard receipts) and make it required when the lot value exceeds ₹50,000 and the vehicle is motorised, or when the movement is inter-state; yards raise bills on the free NIC portal with E-Way Bill 2.0 as the fallback and SMS as the field backup; defer any software recommendation until prices are re-checked.

verdicts.question: Is the MSME 45-day payment rule (MSMED Act s.15–16 and Income-tax s.43B(h)) still in force in 2026, and do Bengaluru yards buying metal from unregistered kabadiwalas issue reverse-charge self-invoices in practice?
verdicts.problems: Same tooling limit: WebSearch budget exhausted and fetches refused, so none of the 18 sources could be re-found from a snippet in this pass. Substantive problems found by cross-checking against the repo's own gazette-backed research and known law: (1) A factual error: the answer says 'plastic, paper, rubber and e-waste scrap are at 5%'. The sibling scrap-tax research (citing the Gazette copy of Notification 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate) of 17 September 2025) places plastic waste and scrap 3915 in Schedule II at 18% (18% since 1 October 2021, Notification 8/2021) and electrical and electronic waste 8549 at 18% (since 18 July 2022, Notification 6/2022); only waste paper 4707, glass cullet 7001, rubber 4004 and rags 6309/6310 are at 5%. The conclusion that only metal scrap of Chapters 72 to 81 is under the Notification 06/2024 reverse charge is still right. (2) 's.37(2)(g) of the Income-tax Act 2025' is not confirmed by any snippet; the sibling research only cites 'section 37' and the sub-section numbering may be wrong. (3) The MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 timeline (introduced 28 July, Rajya Sabha 3 August, Lok Sabha 7 August 2026) and the Rajya Sabha Unstarred Q.242 of 21 July 2026 are after any reference point I can check and rest on TaxGuru/LiveLaw/SAG pages that were not re-found; keep them as reported, with assent still an open item. (4) The source entries again say 'opened 29 Sep 2026' without 'snippet:' prefixes. (5) Arithmetic and mechanics that do check: 45 days/15 days under s.15; s.16 compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate; rule 47A 30-day self-invoice (Notification 20/2024-Central Tax, effective 1 November 2024); Circular 211/5/2024 of 26 June 2024 on the ITC time limit; 2% GST TDS above ₹2.5 lakh per contract (Notification 25/2024-Central Tax, REG-07 registration, confirmed independently by the sibling research). (6) Against the refined chain the answer stops at the kabadiwala-to-yard leg. The metal-scrap RCM applies at any leg where a registered buyer takes Chapter 72 to 81 scrap from an unregistered seller (including a small unregistered yard selling to a pre-processor), the 2% GST TDS applies on registered-to-registered metal legs above ₹2.5 lakh per contract ex-GST (the L3 and L4 legs, not L1/L2), and the separate 2% income-tax TCS on scrap sales (Finance Act 2026, s.394 of the 2025 Act, from 1 April 2026, per the sibling research) is collected by firm/company sellers unless the buyer gives a Form 127 manufacturing declaration, which pre-processors and recyclers can give. Industrial by-products (slag, dross, fly ash, foundry sand: Chapter 26 and others) are outside Chapters 72 to 81, so the metal-scrap RCM and TDS do not attach to them; and once material passes state S7 (ingot, granule) it may no longer be 'waste and scrap' of 7204/7404/7602 at all, which changes the RCM and TCS analysis and needs a CA's view.
verdicts.correction: Both halves are in force. MSMED Act s.15 caps payment to a micro or small enterprise at 45 days from acceptance (15 days if nothing is agreed in writing) and s.16 charges compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate; the tax disallowance for late payment sat in s.43B(h) of the 1961 Act for FY 2025-26 (tax audit due 30 September 2026) and from 1 April 2026 continues in section 37 of the Income-tax Act 2025 (exact clause number not confirmed; the text disallows sums payable to a micro or small enterprise beyond the s.15 time limit until actually paid). Reports of a July 2026 Rajya Sabha reply confirming no relaxation, and of the MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 passing both Houses in August 2026 without touching ss.15 and 16, could not be re-verified in this pass: treat assent and commencement as an open item for the Gazette. The rule only bites on dues to Udyam-registered micro or small enterprises, and traders (most kabadiwalas) get Udyam registration only for priority-sector lending, so they are generally outside it, while a yard, pre-processor, recycler or compounder that processes material can be a manufacturing MSE and is inside it. In the refined chain that means every paying party from L2 upward (yards paying pre-processors, recyclers paying pre-processors or compounders, manufacturers paying recyclers) should capture the seller's Udyam number and pay within 45 days, and Luma.Green itself once it moves money. On GST: Notification 06/2024-Central Tax (Rate), effective 10 October 2024, puts 18% reverse charge on metal scrap of Customs Chapters 72 to 81 bought by any registered person from an unregistered seller, with no threshold, paid in cash and creditable as ITC; the buyer raises a self-invoice within 30 days (rule 47A, Notification 20/2024-Central Tax, from 1 November 2024) and a payment voucher. Rates after 22 September 2025 (Notification 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate)): ferrous 7204, copper/brass 7404, aluminium 7602 and other metal scrap 18%; plastic scrap 3915 18%; e-waste 8549 18%; waste paper 4707, glass cullet 7001, rubber 4004 and rags 6309/6310 5%. Only the Chapter 72 to 81 metal legs carry RCM; plastic, paper, glass and e-waste bought from unregistered sellers carry no GST at all. On registered-to-registered metal legs (typically L3 yard to pre-processor and L4 to manufacturer) the buyer must deduct 2% GST TDS where a contract exceeds ₹2.5 lakh ex-GST (Notification 25/2024-Central Tax, REG-07 registration, GSTR-7). Separately, from 1 April 2026 sellers that are firms or companies collect 2% income-tax TCS on scrap sales unless the buyer gives a Form 127 declaration that the goods are for manufacturing or processing, which pre-processors and recyclers can give. Industrial by-products such as slag, dross, fly ash and foundry sand fall outside Chapters 72 to 81, so neither the metal-scrap RCM nor the metal-scrap GST TDS attaches to them; classify each candidate listing by its own HSN. Whether a lot that has reached S7 (ingot, granule, pellet) is still 'waste and scrap' for RCM and TCS purposes is a question for the CA. Whether Bengaluru yards actually issue self-invoices cannot be settled from public pages; industry and practitioner posts from 2025 to 2026 (not re-verified here) describe uneven compliance. Decision: unchanged for the kabadiwala-to-yard leg (treat every metal purchase from a seller without a GSTIN as RCM and keep a self-invoice-ready register), and extend the same register to every registered buyer in the chain; add a per-contract running total on registered-to-registered metal legs to flag the ₹2.5 lakh GST TDS point; add a Form 127 flag on pre-processor and recycler purchases; correct the material rate table so plastic and e-waste are 18%. Status stays needs-pilot-or-counsel.
